citation: Hanley, J. A. and McNeil, B. J. (1982), The Meaning and Use of the Area under a Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) Curve, Radiology 143(1), 29-36, DOI 10.1148/radiology.143.1.7063747 -- Table I, p. 30, `Rating of 109 CT Images`, a 5 x 2 count table: one reader rated the CT brain images of 109 patients on a five-point suspicion scale, and the two rows give how many of the 58 truly normal and the 51 truly abnormal images fell in each rating.
notes:
THE TRUE DISEASE STATUS OF EACH IMAGE, 1 for abnormal and 0 for normal -- the row a count in Table I sits in. 51 ones and 58 zeros.

TRANSCRIBED AS COUNTS AND EXPANDED HERE, WHICH IS THE ONE THING A READER MUST KNOW. The source prints a 5 x 2 CONTINGENCY TABLE, not 109 records: normal 33/6/6/11/2 and abnormal 3/2/2/11/33 across ratings 1 to 5. The 109 values below are that table expanded cell by cell, rating 1 first and, within each rating, the normal images before the abnormal ones. The expansion is reversible: cross-tabulating this dataset against its sibling reproduces Table I exactly, and no other information has been added. The row ORDER is this file's own -- the paper publishes no patient ordering and none is claimed here.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SUPPORT. There is no patient identifier, no second reader and no covariate: Table I is one reader's ratings and nothing else, so nothing about reader agreement or about the two-reader comparison of the paper's section VI can be checked against it. The smooth binormal area of 0.911 that the paper's p. 32 reports for these data comes from a DIFFERENT estimator -- maximum likelihood under a binormal model -- and is not the empirical area this dataset is here to check.

WHY 0 AND 1 RATHER THAN THE WORDS THE TABLE PRINTS. The conformance harness perturbs a dataset to prove it reached the body, and it moves an INDICATOR column by negating it (tests/conformance/fixtures.py, `is_indicator`). Negating this column swaps the cases and the controls, which turns the area of 0.893 into 0.107 and the case count of 51 into 58.

A column of the strings `normal` and `abnormal` would be moved by appending `~` instead (`move_leaf`), and THIS PARAGRAPH USED TO SAY THE CONTROL WOULD THEN EXAMINE NOTHING. The mechanism is right and the consequence was wrong, in the direction that matters: `~` appended to both levels leaves them in the same sort order, so the case level, the control level and every number stay put -- MEASURED, the area is 0.10682893847194047 before and after and both counts are unchanged -- but `test_a_case_that_ran_moves_when_its_fixture_moves` asserts that the moved payload MUST disagree with the published one, and `controls_level` and `cases_level` are the only fields that moved and are both in this case's `unchecked_keys`. So the case would not sit there quietly passing; it would go RED with an AssertionError saying the body is not reading the dataset.

THE GENERALISATION IS THE OPPOSITE OF SILENT DEATH, AND IT IS WORTH STATING BECAUSE IT REACHES FURTHER THAN THIS FILE. Any oracle case whose only moving input is a string-valued categorical fixture is UN-WRITABLE in this harness rather than vacuous: the harness can move such a column, but not in a way any payload can notice, so the perturbation control refuses the case. The transcription choice below is right; the reason recorded for it was not.
